clue.text: Fleshy feature Dublin Echo put out

indicators.note: put out in the sense of disturbed or upset, so the two place-name words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Irish newspaper publishes something about a fleshy facial feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like the newspaper publishing, but it signals that the letters of DUBLIN ECHO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold of fat under the jaw is a fleshy feature of the face.

clue.text: Stoop pronounced in Hamlet?

indicators.note: pronounced means the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds like it

parts.note: to stoop is to condescend, to deign

explanation.surface: Someone bending down in a performance of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the question mark marks Hamlet as one example of a native of Denmark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Prince Hamlet is from Denmark, an example of a Scandinavian of that nation.

clue.text: Increase risk having finished articles on Lawrence?

parts.note: up as in 'time is up', meaning over
the definite article
the indefinite article
T.E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Someone raises the stakes after writing pieces about Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'articles', supplies two pieces: THE and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise the stake in a poker game is to increase what is at risk.

clue.text: Outcast in force away to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to force away is to repel

explanation.surface: An exile is driven off towards the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A person shunned by society is called a pariah, historically someone with leprosy.

clue.text: Body of vehicle Cameron's aboard

indicators.note: aboard means riding inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
David Cameron, former UK prime minister, is known as Dave

explanation.surface: A former prime minister is on board a car body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; 'Body of vehicle' reads as bodywork, but the definition is just 'Body'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse, a dead body, especially one for dissection.

clue.text: One lacking faith in candidates elevating Democrat

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a letter moves it higher up the word

parts.note: the field is all the runners or candidates in a contest

explanation.surface: A sceptic among election hopefuls promotes a Democratic politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevating' moves the D of FIELD up two places to make FIDEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever, especially one rejecting a particular religion, is someone without faith.

clue.text: Dramatist confident beyond doubt in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: certain, sure

explanation.surface: A playwright speaks with total conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright; in many British accents 'sure' and his surname sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was a famous Irish playwright.

clue.text: One son stuck in burning lift

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside

parts.note: burning means hot
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boy is trapped in a lift that is on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something up, a verb such as hoist or heave.

clue.text: Writer's whereabouts changed with book released

indicators.note: changed means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author's location has altered since a book came out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'released' says the B for book is let go from the letters of WHEREABOUTS before 'changed' rearranges the rest; 'Writer's' is read as 'Writer is'. Keith Waterhouse was an English novelist and journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Waterhouse was an English novelist and playwright, author of Billy Liar.

clue.text: Viking occasionally rushed invading an island?

indicators.note: invading means going inside

parts.note: from John Donne's 'No man is an island'

indicators.note: occasionally means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A Viking raider rushes ashore on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an island?' alludes to John Donne's line that no person is an island; the question mark flags that allusion. 'occasionally' picks alternate letters of 'rushed' and 'invading' puts them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were the Scandinavian raiders and settlers of the Viking age.

clue.text: Assistant brought in well-known stationery

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside

parts.note: noted means famous
PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A secretary is called in to a celebrated stationery shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of paper for jotting things on is an item of stationery.

clue.text: See king in duke's shop

indicators.note: in here says the see-and-king letters sit within the slang word for fists, held as if in a clenched hand

parts.note: dukes is slang for fists
lo is an old word for look or see
R is for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A visitor looks in on the monarch at a nobleman's store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dukes' as fists comes from 'put up your dukes'; the definition takes florist as the shop itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A florist is a shop selling cut flowers and plants.

clue.text: Act involving artist on piano very debauched

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so pieces go inside

parts.note: an act is a deed

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B places A after B

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter plays the piano in a deeply dissolute act.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt and morally degenerate describes a dissolute person.

clue.text: Current passed through lead for instrument

indicators.note: passed through means sent into the middle

parts.note: the lead in a film is its star
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Electricity runs through a lead wire to an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a cable carrying current, but it is the leading actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked Indian lute is a stringed instrument.

clue.text: Overprotective mum kept in Carol

indicators.note: kept in means held inside

parts.note: to carol is to sing
mum is mother

explanation.surface: An overbearing mother keeps her daughter Carol indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name but is the verb to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stifling someone with excessive care is being overprotective.

clue.text: Frightening thing in gym on steroids

indicators.note: in means found within the next words

explanation.surface: A bodybuilder on drugs at the gym is a scary sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying creature or brute is a fearsome thing.

clue.text: Gauche? Play fewer roles after time

indicators.note: after places the play-fewer-roles piece behind the time letter

parts.note: to play is to act
to act fewer roles is to act less

explanation.surface: An awkward actor takes on less work after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking social finesse; awkward and insensitive in manner.

clue.text: Delay arresting university doctor over complaint

indicators.note: arresting means holding inside

parts.note: a lag is a delay
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A hold-up stops an academic medic investigating a medical complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful back ailment is a complaint in the sense of an illness.

clue.text: Hate: it may so spread around province

indicators.note: around means surrounding another piece
spread means the letters are scattered

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is known as the Province

explanation.surface: Hostility may scatter across a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges IT MAY SO into AMOSITY, which goes 'around' NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong hostility or ill-will is a form of hatred.

clue.text: Unusual claret served with ecstasy in syrup

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A strange red wine served alongside a pill tastes like syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is a dark sweet cane syrup.

clue.text: Extremely brainy sort prone to cracking?

definitions.meaning: read literally as a head made of egg, it would easily crack

explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual is a clever person, and literally a head like an egg's shell would break easily.

clue.text: Relatives in BBC succeeded

parts.note: Auntie is the nickname of the BBC

explanation.surface: Family members working at the BBC have done well.
explanation.walkthrough: AUNTIE (or Auntie Beeb) is the British nickname for the BBC, the national broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives, a parent's sisters.

clue.text: Song about endless division in state

indicators.note: about in its sense of round or encircling, so the song wraps around the shortened division

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: a zone is a division of territory

explanation.surface: A song about endless division in a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is a US state in the Southwest.

clue.text: Drawing support and comfort first from lover

parts.note: ease is comfort

indicators.note: first from means take the opening letter

explanation.surface: An artist takes comfort first from a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand holding a canvas or drawing board supports the work.

clue.text: Senior police officer exceptionally good

explanation.definitionFit: Short for superintendent, a high police rank, and also an informal word for excellent.

clue.text: Animal trained to look for an owner?

definitions.text: Animal trained to look for an owner?

parts.words: Animal trained to look for an owner?
parts.note: reads as a pet seeking a home, but means an animal that sees on behalf of its blind owner

explanation.surface: A pet trained to find someone to adopt it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog trained to lead a blind person, acting as its master's eyes.

clue.text: News boss engaging team to do his work?

indicators.note: engaging in the sense of taking on staff: the editor takes the team into his own letters

parts.note: ED, an editor, runs a newspaper
men can be a team

explanation.surface: An editor hires a team to do his job for him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the subject of the clue: correcting copy is the news boss's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Correcting and revising text is what an editor does.

clue.text: Hebridean isle finally approves link by bridge

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: An island in the Hebrides finally agrees a bridge to the mainland.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the real Skye Bridge, opened in 1995.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: Block that is restricting motorway flow

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in

parts.note: IE, id est, means that is
M is a motorway
to pass is to flow along

explanation.surface: Something hinders traffic moving along a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadlock is a block where no progress is possible.

clue.text: Column is penned by warped bloke

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within
warped means twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A newspaper column is written by a twisted man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warped' rearranges BLOKE into OBELK, which 'pens' IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tapering stone pillar is a column monument.

clue.text: Swedish-American star almost in dress

indicators.note: almost means losing the last letter

parts.note: Greta Garbo, the Swedish-born Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A Hollywood legend is nearly wearing a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is clothing or attire.

clue.text: Wife inside had red dye mixed for literary 15 Across

indicators.note: inside means placed within
mixed means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wife's hair is dyed red in a mixed batch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges HAD RED DYE, and W goes 'inside'. 15 Across is MONSTER: Mr Hyde is Stevenson's monstrous creation.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil alter ego of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's novella is a literary fiend.
